title: Strict integral model matching independently of completion units
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l finite, and h:U→T arbitrary. Given any tensor-unit and derived-counit normalized ordinary pullback identification a:PbcProperIntegralPullbackIdentification l E h [def-weil-pbc-proper-integral-ordinary-data], there exists a natural isomorphism b from integralDerivedPullback l E h followed by integralDetailedTransport U l E to integralDetailedTransport T l E followed by completedReductionTower T (pbcIntegralDatum l E), completedTowerPullback h (pbcIntegralDatum l E) and completedTowerRlim (pbcIntegralDatum l E) U. It satisfies PbcProperIntegralModelMatching l E h a b, fixing the entire strict tower augmentation, both Roos coordinates, invertibility of the actual tower counit, and the formula for every entire-tower K-injective resolution with injective terms. No completion-map identity is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4), Remark 6.8.15; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex lemma-derived-limit-is-ok (Tag 0941), proetale.tex Tag 099N(5)

proof.text: Use the natural unit-normalized strict tower isomorphism t on good complexes. Scalar restriction along the unique coefficient isomorphism is an equivalence. The proved scalarRoosMap comparison is therefore a natural isomorphism. Compose it with Roos(t inverse); the scalar comparison projection equations and naturality of the Roos coordinates prove both required coordinates.

Scalar restriction along the unique CommRing lift of the published coefficient isomorphism preserves K-flatness. Apply the completed reduction tower counit computation and the exact tower pullback counit computation to prove invertibility of the actual tower counit on every good representative.

Compose the localized ordinary pullback comparison, Q(z), and the universal normalized Roos comparison with the inverse actual tower counit. Descend this natural isomorphism along good-complex localization using its fully faithful precomposition functor. The descent equation and cancellation of the actual tower counit reduce the required formula for every entire-tower resolution to the Roos normalization formula.

proof_origin.place: M5: original step 1 retained as a strictly tower-level substatement; all cone, counit, resolution and localization descent steps implemented with existing APIs. Stacks 03D3, 06YY, 0941 and 099N(5).

mathlib_searches.query: For a ring sheaf isomorphism restriction of scalars identifies the derived pullback and transports the strict quotient tower Roos cone and completion augmentation
mathlib_searches.results: msearch returned 8 results: ordinary ModuleCat, SheafOfModules and PresheafOfModules restriction of scalars, restriction objects, reflection of isomorphisms and the scalar pseudofunctor. None provides the normalized comparison.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Basic scalar restriction only; does not state this coefficient-normalized assertion.

mathlib_searches.results: 12 results including leftAdjointUniq and its unit and counit equations.
mathlib_searches.verdict: Useful tool for the module isomorphism; does not give the coefficient square, derived counit or normalized tower comparison.

mathlib_searches.query: Restriction of scalars along a ring sheaf isomorphism commutes with derived pullback and the strict inverse limit completion unit
mathlib_searches.results: 8 results about pullback of free modules, pullbackObjUnitToUnit and the composite adjunction conjugate.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No matching derived or strict tower comparison.

mathlib_searches.results: No Mathlib hits for Roos/strict completion augmentation. The second search finds abstract derived-functor comparison isomorphisms and basic scalar-restriction isomorphisms. Local library search finds the existing interfaces and the parent obligation but no theorem for this individual normalization step. Blueprint searches for integral pullback identification, strict model comparison and completion matching each return zero matches.
mathlib_searches.verdict: The existing general tools do not directly state this assertion; no duplicate node found.

mathlib_searches.query: In an abelian category with exact countable products the shifted mapping cone of one minus transition computes the derived inverse limit of a strict tower with its zero-coordinate augmentation
mathlib_searches.results: Eight general cochain mapping-cone and complex-limit formulas; no normalized strict Roos or derived-limit comparison.
mathlib_searches.verdict: These component formulas do not supply the required strict normalization.

from.place: Integral-lattice proof paragraph: identification of ordinary integral pullback and the actual quotient-tower completion comparison; original ordinary-input proof steps 5–7. Parent comparison step(s) 2–3.

lean.statement:
theorem pbc_integral_strict_model_matching_exists
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] {U T : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ T)
    (a : PbcProperIntegralPullbackIdentification l E h) :
    ∃ b : integralDerivedPullback l E h ⋙ integralDetailedTransport U l E ≅
        integralDetailedTransport T l E ⋙ completedReductionTower T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
          completedTowerPullback h (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
            completedTowerRlim (pbcIntegralDatum l E) U,
      PbcProperIntegralModelMatching l E h a b
